chapter: Entertainers, Creole Serenaders and La Vida
title: Origin of the name La Vida, the owner, and substituting at the Budweiser
summary: They discuss the name and owner of La Vida, how Handy hired him, and his Saturday work at the Budweiser.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What did the name La Vida come from? Was that the name of the man who owned the place?
It was a Jew.
That was his name? No, it wasn't his name.
Do you know where it comes from, Jeff? It means the life. Who was that? It means the life. It means the life. In what language? In Spanish.
Oh, I'm trying to think of this man.
It means fast life, you know, prostitution and all that.
Yeah, I knew he was a Jew. He ran his place there.
We can look it up. Yeah.
It was the same man who ran it all the time when you were there. Well yeah, that's the same man.
That's the only one. That was the end of it.
You played until the thing closed down. Until the thing closed down, yeah.
I didn't know if it was up now. No, no, no. It was already playing and Handy hired me.
Who was playing that before you? What band was it before you?
I don't know what band was playing.
You came in with a new band. I came in with Handy.
You see, Louis Kiffin was playing with Handy at the time. He had some kind of falling out in the audience.
And you mentioned the Budweiser too.
Well I used to go and substitute the Budweiser after Artel, which would rest him up a lot of
times. And then in the 90s?
That was after, you know, I left and started working for the Power of Life Company. Then I used to go there and rest on Saturday nights like that, Sunday.
